correctness.rationale: The projected full/target-avoiding Markov transition kernel is exact: for J=H∩U, pure-death comparison has eigenvalues 1-|A|/r on incidence-zeta basis. Uniform finite-dimensional resolvent isolation works because r/n->0. Stationary entrance flux for one fixed s-set is exactly binom(r-1,s-1)/binom(n,s); overlapping targets produce relative O(r/n) loss. Excursions from the empty projected state and first-return transform yield 1-rho=d beta/M [1+O_{s,d}(r/n)], for any fixed d uniformly over target intersections. The condition (r/n) log M->0 and t/r sufficiently large give fixed factorial moments, then Poisson/Gumbel; union-bound geometric tails give E[T]. I reconstructed the rate/scaling and regenerative steps, and independently matched 30 exact full-versus-killed-projection probabilities on n=9,r=4,s=2 with two overlapping targets. Finite checks do not prove the uniform triangular-array estimates.
